📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England Under-21s won Euro 2025 with an extra-time win in Slovakia against Germany.

Lee Carsley has urged his England Under-21s to create a legacy as they aim for a third straight European title.

The Young Lions - who have won the past two European Championships in 2023 and 2025 under Carsley - have been drawn in Group A against France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia at Euro 2027.

Only Italy have won three successive European Under-21 tournaments - between 1992 and 1996 - but that was when just eight teams competed at the finals and not the current 16.

Head coach Carsley told BBC Sport: "The players I am privileged to coach and work with have a great opportunity to make history with three in a row in this format and create their own legacy within the under-21s.".

He was speaking after Thursday's draw in Belgrade, with Serbia hosting the tournament with Albania.

"This group of players are in a really unique position and it will be a while before another group will be in this position," mentioned Carsley.

"Let's go for it. Why not? Go all out to try to win it. That's what we're going to do. We have the players who can do that.

In a recent development, "They are highly motivated. We have seen that in the last two tournaments we have had, the players were so determined to win every game and it makes it a lot easier from a coaching point of view.".

England will open their campaign against France - who they beat 3-2 in Bristol last week - on 16 June in Leskovac before facing Serbia in Belgrade on 19 June.

The Young Lions stay in the Serbian capital for their final group game against Poland on Tuesday, 22 June.

England U21s boss Carsley keen to handle Dowman with care.

Industry News: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function.
  • Industry observers note that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less vital than how they use that time.
  • The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.

Industry observers note that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less vital than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.

These questions are especially vital because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.

More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills.

One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.

Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn fresh things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.

The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.

"The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.

"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.

Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently.

The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.

Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.

Industry observers note that working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing newly introduced information.

According to recent reports, light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.

In a recent development, the differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.

Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity.

According to recent reports, the study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.

Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.

Sources indicate that one possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.

This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.

"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.

Sources indicate that "However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is crucial to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing.".

What the Eight-Year Study Revealed.

The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.

According to recent reports, the current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.

In a recent development, researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.

To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.

Sources indicate that importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.

In a recent development, nevertheless, the results offer an notable perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.

The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.

Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.

The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joan Smalls is strutting away from relationships that don't respect girl code.

One month after rumors emerged that the Victoria's Secret supermodel was unhappy with fellow runway star Candice Swanepoel for dating her former fling Tom Brady, she confirmed the Fresh England Patriots alum was at the center of their friendship breakup.

"Unfortunately, that was the catalyst," Smalls mentioned during the Nov. 25 episode of The Cutting Room Floor podcast. "I was seeing this person for a period of eight months.".

According to recent reports, E! News has reached out to reps for Swanepoel and Brady for comment and has not yet heard back.

Though Smalls doesn't consider Brady to be an ex, she clarified that they casually dated the former NFL star on and off between 2023 and 2024. Swanepoel went on to spark romance rumors with Brady in June.

And for her part, Smalls emphasized that before ending her and Swanepoel's 15-year friendship—which she confirmed took place in April—they were each other's confidants about love and heartbreak.

"You've seen the relationships, situationships and people I've dated, and I've confided in you in these spaces and we never had a crossover," she reflected. "All of a sudden, I stopped seeing this person, and three months later, you text me and say, 'Oh, we have to speak about something,' which is usually not a conversation we normally have.".

The Puerto Rican-born model—who had confirmed their fallout in scathing comments under her own Instagram posts last month—had a feeling that Swanepoel, 38, was planning to name him her MVP.

According to recent reports, "I called her and I asked her, I said, 'Is this about him?' She said, 'Yes,'" she recalled. "We spoke on the phone very briefly, and I was just perplexed and lost for words.".

The confrontation was especially devastating because Smalls remarked Swanepoel—who was previously linked to model Andrés Velencoso in 2022—had been a guiding light during her romance with the Fox Sports commentator.

"She helped me write text messages to this person," Smalls, also 38, stated. "She knew intimate things. Potentially to my detriment, I overshared. I was just being open with a friend that I thought was a safe spac.

As for how the conversation went? Smalls accused her former friend of committing a cardinal girl code sin: Dating a guy your friend was romantically involved with.

"She came across as justifying her actions," she explained. "She started diminishing my experience to make herself feel better about the situation, which I think is what infuriated me.".

Smalls believed that Swanepoel—who shares two sons with ex Hermann Nicoli—refused to take accountability for being a bad friend.

"It was this whole attitude of 'I'm an adult. I don't need permission,'" she posited. "Both are actually true: you are an adult and you don't need permission. But as a friend, you should consider me in your choices. Don't consider me in your apologies.".

Recent findings suggest that "Then she was like, 'Well, I'm sorry, but I'm going to explore this and so is life,'" she continued. "It was just this attitude of entitlement and lack of care towards someone who's your friend and something that I would never do to you.".

Looking back at the conversation, Smalls felt that Swanepoel was looking to ease her own mind.

As she put it, "She wanted me to comfort her about her bad decision so that she didn't feel guilty by her choice and then she would constantly justify it.".

It was especially difficult for the model since she prefers to keep her inner circle small.

"I rarely allow people into my life, and I'm very private," Smalls added. "So, if I let you into a space that I thought you would protect me as my friend, that's the only one thing I asked for you to do. Create a safe space for me to be myself, to open up, and you can't do that.".

Following initial speculations about their fallout, Swanepoel's team detailed her perspective on their friendship.

"Candice has always been exceptionally private about her personal life, with her focus remaining on raising her children," her rep Amanda Ruisi told E! News in October. "She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect.".

After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance.

A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history.

As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday, was a “massive joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute.

Wesley Fofana played all 90 minutes of Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United on Saturday.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicates defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.

Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool.

He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso stated the matter was now "closed".

"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," remarked the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest.

Sources indicate that "We are here to take things seriously. He's mentioned it will not be repeated. We don't want these kind of things and they won't be repeated.".

Alonso refused to confirm whether Fofana had been punished by the club, but mentioned "we have addressed that with him.".

Interviewer defends Fofana after backlash.

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea.

'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over.

Fofana's comments followed criticism from fans of his performances this season, including in last weekend's humiliation at the hands of historic rivals Leeds.

But interviewer Nani defended Fofana against the backlash, saying: "People can clearly see he wasn't happy. He admits he didn't play well and claims he needs to improve.".

The interviewer also defended Fofana's explanation for putting himself forward to take a penalty against Liverpool, saying the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch.

The 25-year-old France defender has often struggled for form and fitness since completing a Â£70m move from Leicester City in August 2022.

He has made 81 appearances for the club in four years, but has played nine times under new manager Alonso this season.

In that time Chelsea have struggled with defensive frailty, conceding 20 goals in their 11 Premier League games.

They are eighth in the table after falling to a third defeat in their last four league matches.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.

The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.

You can read details on what has been happening at the top football club in this DW article: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has mentioned.

The family said in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later said in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

In a recent development, according to his family, Flick once remarked: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

Sources indicate that "Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It said the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an vital bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG stated it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an important shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," said Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also stated that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It mentioned species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig indicates that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

Recent findings suggest that "Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she said, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She said that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), remarked she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She stated that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are presently being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

The powerful IG Metall union mentioned on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding firm Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union noted that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It states that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

The DW newsroom says "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.

Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.

In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.

And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has mentioned it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.

Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.

Sources indicate that we're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!

A new goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

In a recent development, after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

In a recent development, however, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke mentioned he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

Sources indicate that fourth-place RB Leipzig had five different players score in a 5-1 victory over Union Berlin, bringing them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen scored four unanswered goals against Paderborn to stay in fifth place.

Germany is seeking to redress years of underinvestment by pouring billions into the modernization of public infrastructure and digital networks, and the transition to renewable energy sources.

But will the strategy bring real change amid the labor shortages, burdensome bureaucracy and low productivity presently besetting Europe's largest economy?

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

Operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

Bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

According to recent reports, "We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen mentioned. "This demonstrates that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

It has been revealed that moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer said.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

Bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the important matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism.
  • It has been revealed that the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal vital differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
  • The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism. Although adults with and without autism showed remarkably similar brain activity when researchers compared group averages, a closer examination uncovered striking differences between individuals. These differences were especially pronounced in brain regions involved in understanding and responding to social information.

It has been revealed that the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal vital differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The discovery could help scientists better understand why autism varies so widely from person to person and eventually support more personalized approaches to care.

The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.

What Brain Scans Reveal When People Watch Movies.

To explore these differences, the team examined previously collected brain imaging data from Indiana University and Caltech. The recordings captured brain activity as adults with and without autism watched movies from several genres, including animation, action, romantic comedy, and Hitchcockian thrillers.

Sources indicate that movies offered researchers a way to study how the brain responds to a constantly changing stream of sights, sounds, and social interactions. Unlike simple laboratory tasks, movies present a rich mixture of information that more closely resembles the complexity of everyday experiences.

Using the imaging data, the researchers trained a computational model to identify connections between brain activity and different elements of the movies. These included visual details, sounds, and more abstract social information, such as interactions between characters.

After training, the model was able to accurately predict activity across several brain systems.

Kliemann explained why this approach is particularly useful for investigating the social challenges sometimes associated with autism: "The computational model allowed us to look for robust brain responses to many different aspects of the complex, dynamic contexts in the movies.".

A Surprising Difference Hidden by Brain Activity Averages.

The most unexpected finding emerged when researchers compared the two groups.

At first, the results suggested relatively little difference. When brain responses were averaged across participants, the model predicted activity in various brain systems similarly for adults with and without autism.

However, the picture changed when the researchers examined how much individual participants differed from others in their own group.

People with autism indicated substantially greater variation in their brain responses than participants without autism. In other words, although the overall group averages looked similar, the responses of individual autistic participants were much less alike.

Sources indicate that this increased variability appeared across nearly every brain system examined. The strongest differences occurred in the social brain system, a network of regions involved in processing social information and understanding other people.

Why the Findings Could Change Autism Research.

According to recent reports, the results raise important questions about how scientists investigate autism. Many existing approaches to understanding and treating the condition rely heavily on comparing average measurements from groups of autistic and nonautistic individuals.

But if autistic people show considerable differences in how their brains process information, these averages may obscure some of the most meaningful findings.

Industry observers note that traer described the team's surprise: "We were surprised by the similarity of group averages. The results suggest that we need to focus on understanding the details of individual brain responses. How and why do they differ?".

Rather than searching only for brain activity patterns shared by everyone with autism, the findings point toward the potential value of studying individuals and identifying smaller groups with similar characteristics.

Kliemann highlighted what this could mean for future research and support: "Identifying ASD subgroups may help us build a more precise understanding of the condition and help develop ways to provide individually tailored support.".

The researchers now strategy to investigate how these differences in brain activity relate to variations in autism-related behavior. They hope to determine where and when the differences emerge, how they are connected to individual characteristics, and what might explain them.

Ultimately, the findings suggest that understanding autism may require looking beyond the average brain and paying closer attention to the distinctive ways individuals process the world.

Materials provided by Society for Neuroscience. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Leeds do not give much away at the back either, though, and I think that will be key in this game.

When I watch Coventry they are dynamic with their counter-attacks and I always fancy them to nick a goal like that.

Industry observers note that not this time, however. Leeds might take a while to break them down, but I think they will come out on top.

According to recent reports, nathan's prediction: Coventry play in sky blue too? Part of the reason I became a Manchester City fan was the kit, and I have always gravitated towards teams in light blue, so I am going to go with Coventry here. 0-1.

I am at this game for 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United.

Industry observers note that no-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble.

United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season.

Industry observers note that that was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test.

The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway.

Pochettino needs something to cling to, but for him picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey. Whoever he picks, they are not very good.

I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment.

Nathan's prediction: It is tough for me to talk about United because in America we have a saying 'don't kick a man when he's down' and it's pretty rough for them right now... but I'm not going to lie, it is nice to see United this low in the table.

I don't think it is the manager that is the problem for United right now, so I don't think Pochettino coming in is going to be an instant fix. They've got some growing pains to get through, and I won't be disappointed to watch that.

When I watch the Premier League at home, Brentford always cracks me up because I am huge fan of The Office and I just imagine a bunch of David Brents out there, just running around the pitch, which is a very funny thing for me.

I know I just said don't kick a man when he's down, but I don't think United would be nice to us if we were down there... so, I think the David Brents are going to win. 1-2.

I actually think Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan.

Sources indicate that I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him.

Recent findings suggest that ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull and Coventry both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides.

That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three.

I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six in all competitions, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here.

Nathan's prediction: Villa have had some surprising results recently but I do think they will win this. 1-3.

I was in Bruges to watch Liverpool in midweek and it was interesting to see two of their players who came in for some heavy flak last season, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both shine.

Isak is looking like the player who Liverpool thought they signed in 2025. He is finding his rhythm, and Wirtz also seems to be in a really good place confidence-wise. When I watch them now, it feels like something is going to happen.

In a recent development, there are other positives for Reds boss Andoni Iraola too. I know there will be a debate about Bradley Barcola's end-product but I love watching him in full flow when he is running past defenders - there is no better sight in football than moments like that.

Rio Ngumoha is exciting as well, and he has such a good football brain which makes him even more dangerous.

Everything points to a Liverpool win, but I am hesitant to just go with that because Everton are coming off the back of a drubbing by Brentford. You can imagine David Moyes giving his side a miserable old week and getting stuck into his players.

It has been revealed that I didn't think James Tarkowski should have been sent off in that game, but he will be suspended here. It is his absence that swings it for me because he is a real leader for Everton.

Nathan's prediction: Everton are usually the underdogs in this game but both teams are pretty level at the moment. One of our record producers is a huge Liverpool fan so he won't be happy with me... but I am going to say Everton will take it. 2-1.

I was at Newcastle's draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward.

Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don't think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him.

Brighton probably still can't believe they lost to Hull last week - but lightning is not going to strike twice.

In a recent development, nathan's prediction: I have to give a shout out to my statistician Lucy here, because there were a couple of teams I didn't know a lot about and she gave me some good insight. So, Brighton have scored a lot of goals this season and I think they will get more here. 3-1.

It has been revealed that thomas Frank has got a huge task at Crystal Palace. They are conceding so many goals.

Losing Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi from their defence was like Robbie Williams and Jason Orange leaving Take That, because they were never going to be the same without them.

I still think Frank has got some decent attacking players, however.

The Hull keeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, looks like a great signing. I don't know how he made some of his saves against Brighton and he probably doesn't know himself either.

Brighton should have buried them and I think Palace will get plenty of chances too.

Fair play to Hull for their spirit and the way they scrap for each other, but I still think they are going to go down.

Hull fans are probably wondering if I am ever going to predict they will win a game... the answer is no, at least not this week anyway.

Nathan's prediction: Palace have given up 27 goals in 11 games which is a lot. Hull have surprised a few people this season and I am backing them here. 0-2.

Bournemouth are on a long winning run in the league but I've been impressed by Fulham whenever I've watched them.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side have not been great at home, with only one win at Craven Cottage so far, so I am going with them to get another draw - which would be their fourth in a row.

Nathan's prediction: Both these teams have picked up a lot, so this is a tough one to call. 2-2.

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi must think a lot of 18-year-old midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett after picking him for their win over Ipswich.

I love to see managers trust young players like that, especially because Spurs have had such a tricky season so far.

It will be interesting to see whether De Zerbi picks him again here, but I feel like the outcome of this game is more dependent on which Sunderland we see.

They picked up a good point at Villa last time out, but they never seem to be quite the same after they have played in Europe, like they are doing this week.

The Black Cats will be without injured duo Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for this game too, so I don't think they will have enough to win it.

In a recent development, nathan's prediction: Dave Stewart from Eurythmics lives in Nashville too and is a good buddy of mine - and he is Sunderland until death! He is such a die-hard fan that every time we have dinner, we will sit there and talk about 'Haway the Lads' and just shoot the breeze about Sunderland.

So I am going to back them in this one, because of Dave and also because of my neighbour Jeremy, who I mentioned earlier.

Sources indicate that jeremy was especially cocky when they had Harry Kane and he would just talk so much smack - I always knew if they were doing good because I'd get a text from him. So, because Jeremy is such a cocky little Spurs fan, I am saying Sunderland will win. 2-1.

I always enjoy this game because of Gabriel's battle with Erling Haaland, but it is in midfield where I think it will be decided.

Manchester City have spent a lot of money on players in that part of the pitch but Enzo Maresca has not found the right combination yet.

Somehow Maresca has got to find a way of nullifying Declan Rice, but that will be very difficult because Rice is just an absolute machine.

You can never rule City out because of Haaland's ability to score goals but the only result I see here is an Arsenal win, and I am going for a classic Gunners scoreline.

Nathan's prediction: This is the major one! It's huge. I feel really good about it, too. Arsenal are riding so high at the moment, I feel like we might catch them snoozing.

Recent findings suggest that I predict Haaland will get two goals, Phil Foden will get one too and we will end up with four. 2-4.

After drawing a blank since week two, Chris finally picked up another win in week 11 - and it was his spot-on prediction for Liverpool to thump Manchester United 4-0 that sealed the deal.

That meant he got three correct results, including two exact scores - at Anfield, and Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich - giving him a total of 90 points.

In a tricky week for predictions, where Liverpool were the only team to start the weekend in the Premier League's top six who won, it was those exact scores that made all the difference.

Chris' guest, undisputed world champion boxer Lauren Price, the BBC readers and AI also all got three correct results.

But the BBC readers were the only ones to also get an exact score - in the Spurs game - giving them 60 points.

Lauren and AI both ended up on 30 points - AI did call Newcastle's draw with Arsenal correctly, but it was wrong about Bournemouth's win over Nottingham Forest, which everyone else got right.

Not many of you got that Liverpool-United scoreline correct, either.

From around 27,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline picked was a 2-1 home win and only 570 of you went for 4-0.

"When has AI ever gone for a 4-0?" mentioned Sutton. "That's what the crowd wants. The crowd don't want AI - who wants mathematics?

"The crowd want gut-feeling and instinct. I think I should get 1,000 points for that prediction, because I was brave enough to go for it.".

For the first time this season, there were SIX games where no-one made a correct prediction - who thought it was easy?

The biggest shock of the week was Leeds' 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Again from around 27,000 predictions, more than 3,600 (14%) of you did back Daniel Farke's side to win... but just 11 of you saw that scoreline coming.

‘Blade Runner 2099’ cast praise the incredible set designs that brought the sci-fi universe to life: ‘it was all so well-realized’ (interview)

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prime Video’s "Blade Runner 2099" has arrived with an 8-episode limited series revealing what the "Blade Runner" world looks like 50 years after the events of director Denis Villeneuve’s "Blade Runner 2049.".

The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens.

Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode.

We connected with three of the sci-fi show’s main co-stars, Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon"), Lewis Gribben ("T2 Trainspotting") and Dimitri Abold ("Love Addicts") to hear more about working with creator/showrunner Silka Louisa, and immersing themselves in "Blade Runner 2099's" vivid futuristic worldbuilding.

"For me it's a lot simpler than egos because he's such a goal-oriented person and all of his stuff has such a police procedural quality to it," Needham tells SPACE regarding his role as Yahya, an emotionless replicant who despises all humans.

"It was really fun to just follow what Silka [Louisa] did. She wrote this great, really exciting mystery thriller, and I just got to play in that.”.

Scottish actor Gribben portrays Cora's ailing younger brother Elias, who has compromised mobility and a rocky relationship with his overprotective sister.

"I've played a few characters that were fairly vulnerable or insular," he notes. "Then seeing the journey of this character grow in strength and confidence and feel like becoming his own man was so compelling to me. It’s almost a relationship that falls apart between brother and sister, and that's fascinating to me because that’s such a cool dynamic you don’t always really see in television highlights. That was quite interesting and made me want to try and be in it.".

According to recent reports, as Bebeto, a doctor, veteran of the replicants vs. humans war, and a black-market dealer helping his species procure IDs and passports off-world, Abold enjoyed exploring the many facets of his character.

"Much like Matthew and Lewis, for me it was the journey that Bebeto goes on," Abold adds. "Starting out as someone who’s so hopeful and has to try and scrape up the last dregs of hope as things start falling apart. Being subject to circumstances like that inherently make for an interesting story arc and story in general. Throwing myself into that, especially after how well Silka crafted the story and script, was something I was totally ready for.".

"Blade Runner 2099’s" sets and locations feature detailed production design that allowed the actors to experience a seamless transition into the complex shoot.

"For me and Dimitri, our first day was in Bebeto’s apartment, and it was all so well-realized,” Gribben recalls.

In a recent development, "You saw all the gadgets because obviously Bebeto was a bit of a tinkerer of a character and had lots of machinery and works and stuff. It took up about 70% of the acting, and we just had to come with compelling conviction. It made it so easy. When you audition for these things, you feel like you have to act more because you’re in a blue screen vacuum. But then you’re there, and it’s so visually well created like that, it made it so easy to be immersed in it.".

"Blade Runner 2099" is at the moment airing all 8 episodes exclusively on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the WWE star called out how the sport's fan base puts undue pressure on its female performers "to walk through that curtain and be perfect," she shaved her head in an emotional display in the ring following an alopecia diagnosis in August.
  • "I'm sure you can all imagine how afraid I was to share with the world that at 23 years old, I was diagnosed with alopecia," Hail tearfully confessed during the Nov.
  • In a recent development, and the wrestler admitted that losing 40 percent of her hair in less than four months made her fearful about her future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thea Hail isn't defined by her hair.

As the WWE star called out how the sport's fan base puts undue pressure on its female performers "to walk through that curtain and be perfect," she shaved her head in an emotional display in the ring following an alopecia diagnosis in August.

"I'm sure you can all imagine how afraid I was to share with the world that at 23 years old, I was diagnosed with alopecia," Hail tearfully confessed during the Nov. 24 WWE NXT broadcast, "an autoimmune condition that causes you to lose your hair.".

In a recent development, and the wrestler admitted that losing 40 percent of her hair in less than four months made her fearful about her future. As she explained, "I'd love to sit here and lie to you guys and tell you that I was super optimistic about this all, but I wasn't.".

She noted that her upcoming normal had her especially worried about how she would be judged if her hair never grew back.

Sources indicate that "Since July, I've been asking myself the same questions you're all probably wondering," Hail continued. "Most importantly, 'How will other people look at me if I have no hair?'".

As such, her ongoing feud with WWE costar Chantel Monroe, who has frequently used Hail's bald patches as a part of their scripted confrontations on the program, has been difficult for Hail.

Recent findings suggest that "Chantel gave me that answer really quickly, and she proved just about every fear I had to be true," she shared. "She made me feel so small and so defeated as a part of my life that I wasn't ready to share was exposed by somebody else.".

In addition, she called out the beauty standard she feels gets held against women in the ring for looking anything from "too muscular" to "too skinny.".

"Do you know how long every girl back there sits in the hair and makeup chair before they come out here just so you all don't tear them to shreds?" she questioned. "Because God forbid their extensions don't blend the way that you think they should, or their tan's a little weird, or you don't like their gear.".

With that in mind, Hail aimed "to take this moment of weakness and turn it into a strength" to convey how her alopecia has become "a bit of a blessing in disguise.".

Ultimately, the Pittsburgh native was all smiles as she ended her heartfelt speech by shaving off her mane with an electric razor while the crowd chanted her name.

According to recent reports, hail first shared her journey with alopecia in an Aug. 27 Instagram, captioned, "i now have alopecia areata… i have literally manifested going bald.".

Read on for more stars who have been vulnerable about their health.

Travis Barker's Precancer Diagnosis.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus.".

Recent findings suggest that "I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Substantial Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor said it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking.".

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

Recent findings suggest that "The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months.".

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she remarked her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time.".

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better.".

According to recent reports, "Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much.".

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst.

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

Industry observers note that "There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood.".

Nikki Garcia's Breast Implant Injury.

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

"It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'".

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed.".

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain.".

In a recent development, "It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked.".

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

"This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first.".

Lupita Nyong'o's Uterine Fibroids.

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

According to recent reports, "When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most.".

Brian Austin Green's Perforated Appendix.

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

Recent findings suggest that “Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian remarked in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”.

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”.

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

It has been revealed that "'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?".

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game.

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

It has been revealed that the United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

Industry observers note that “Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert.".

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident.

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine noted in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”.

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it.".

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he remarked on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”.

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”.

Matt Kirschenheiter's Heart Attack.

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

Tracy Morgan's Medical Emergency.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an patch on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

Christy Carlson Romano's Eye Injury.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

Recent findings suggest that "There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye.".

Recent findings suggest that the Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment).".

Recent findings suggest that the actress remarked she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant.".

It has been revealed that while the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors remarked they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable.".

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade.

In a recent development, the AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, Upcoming Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent.".

Industry observers note that hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey noted the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

Justin Bieber's Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine.".

Jamie Foxx's Brain Bleed & Stroke.

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I noted, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”.

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser.

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”.

According to recent reports, “My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”.

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent.".

Recent findings suggest that snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine.".

Shailene Woodley's Health Battle.

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".
